provenance.note: Content digests rather than a commit id, so the register is reproducible from the commit that contains it. No timestamp is recorded.

meaning.scope: Repository evidence only: which routes have a tracked caller in this repository. It does not show which routes are used in production.
meaning.usageEvidence: NOT_COLLECTED for every route. No deployment or access-log evidence has been gathered (R5-C2 onwards). Retiring an endpoint requires 90 days of production access-log evidence and owner review.
meaning.externalConsumerStatus: UNKNOWN for every route. Repository evidence cannot prove that no external consumer exists.
meaning.retirementStatus: EVIDENCE_REQUIRED: no tracked active caller and no operator-retain annotation; needs access-log evidence and owner review before any decision. NOT_AUTHORIZED: no retirement is authorised. No record is ever marked safe to delete.

classifications.ACTIVE_TRACKED_CALLER: A request site in reachable client code whose enclosing function is itself used, not merely located in a reachable module.
classifications.BROWSER_GENERATED_PATH: The API (or active client code) builds this URL for the browser to load directly, e.g. a signed private-file link; there is no axios/fetch call.
classifications.SERVER_INTERNAL_CALLER: The API calls this route itself.
classifications.UNUSED_EXPORT: A request site in a reachable module whose function nothing active uses, including helpers called only by unused siblings.
classifications.UNREACHABLE_CALLER: A request site in client code not reachable from client/src/index.js, or used only from such code. Not an active caller.
classifications.TEST_ONLY: Only automated tests call it. Tests show expected behaviour, not deployed consumption.
classifications.OPERATOR_RETAIN: Explicit reviewed annotation: an operator or security endpoint kept regardless of frontend callers.
classifications.NO_TRACKED_ACTIVE_CALLER: No active client caller, browser-generated path or server caller in the repository. Not evidence that production does not use it.
classifications.EXTERNAL_CONSUMER_POSSIBLE: Public or optional-auth route, or no tracked caller: an external consumer cannot be ruled out from the repository.
classifications.UNKNOWN: Reserved for evidence the analysis cannot attribute; call sites it cannot resolve are listed under unresolvedCallSites.

meaning.matching: Client URLs are resolved through module constants, local variables, API base constants (process.env.X || "/api" resolves to its literal default; no environment value is read) and the same-file call sites of wrapper functions. A runtime value fills one path segment and matches only a route parameter, never a static segment such as /public or /tree. The first route registered in Express order wins. Each HTTP method is a separate record. Browser-generated URLs are GET.
meaning.ordering: Records sorted by path, then method. Evidence sites sorted by file, then line.

summary.note: Counts overlap: a route can carry several classifications.

handler.label: async (req, res) => { const user = await User.findById(req.user.id) .select("fullName email role isActive lastLoginAt createdAt clientId avatarUrl avatarMediaId team jobTitle phone notificationPreferences") .lean(); if (!user) return res.status(404).json({ ok: false, message: "User not found" }); return res.json({ ok: true, user }); }

async (req, res) => { const ALLOWED = ["fullName", "phone", "jobTitle", "avatarUrl", "avatarMediaId"]; const patch = {}; ALLOWED.forEach((k) => { if (req.body[k] !== undefined) patch[k] = req.body[k]; }); const user = await User.findByIdAndUpdate(req.user.id, patch, { new: true, runValidators: true }) .select("fullName email role isActive team jobTitle phone avatarUrl"); return res.json({ ok: true, user }); }
